events.event_hazard: Nuclear disaster at Fukushima Daiichi triggered by earthquake and tsunami
key_impacts: Reactor fuel melted inside the nuclear reactors.
Extremely contaminated cooling water leaked into reactor building basements.
About 400 tons/day of groundwater inflow led to extensive on-site storage of contaminated water in large tanks.
Ongoing cooling is required to prevent further radioactive releases.
evidence_snippets: Large-scale nuclear disaster at TEPCO’s Fukushima Daiichi, directly caused by the Great East Japan Earthquake and Tsunami of March 11, 2011.
Nuclear fuel that melted inside the nuclear reactors due to the accident.
About 400 tons of groundwater flow in daily; contaminated water leaked into basements and is stored in large tanks on site.
missing_information: Casualty and evacuation figures not provided.
Directly affected surrounding towns/settlements not specified.
Precise timelines of subsequent releases and storage operations not detailed.
